the sequential culture of human embryos in serum-free medium has resulted in the production of blastocysts with a high implantation rate.

sequential culture of human embryos in serum-free media can result in a high implantation rate, that this can be achieved by replacing serum with the glycosminoglycan hyauluronate, and that non-invasive tests for embryo viability will facilitate the transfer of only the most competent embryos.
sequential serum-free culture of human embryos in vitro can produce blastocysts with a 50% implantation rate.

the development of sequential culture systems which will support the growth of viable human blastocytes.
the development of culture conditions for the human preimplantation stage embryo.

, in human IVF and in other mammalian IVF, there is no evidence that culture in serum-free media is detrimental to embryo development and that, in fact, the use of such media is associated with improved embryo development and viability.

the culture of human embryos beyond the cleavage stage to the blastocyst will improve the efficiency of human IV, increase the viability of embryos transferred and reduce the number of embryos transferred to establish a pregnancy.

the culture of human embryos in serum-free sequential medium is a reliable, efficient, safe and inexpensive method for producing blastocysts.
the culture of viable blastocysts is possible and will be a significant step in improving the overall efficiency of the human IVF programme.
, with the development of sequential serum-free culture media, we have been able to culture viable human blastocyst stage embryos and that these have resulted in a high implantation rate.

human embryos are very sensitive to changes in their environment, particularly during the period of implantation.

the use of defined, serum-free media for the culture of human embryos is possible, and the use of sequential media for blastocyst culture is likely to increase implantation rate and reduce the number of embryos required for transfer.
